samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copies the source's comment threads for sheet/slides/board, violating the documented "comments are not carried over" invariant
samples.evidence: `copyContent` copies every key of the source root verbatim for `sheet`/`slides`/`board` (`for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(snapshot))`). Spreadsheet comment threads live *inside* that root: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-6` stores them at `ws.comments`, and `yorkie-store.ts:285,495,687` shows `ws` is `root.sheets[tabId]`. So a copied sheet carries all comment threads (bodies, author usernames, ids), directly contradicting the service's own doc comment ("Comments, share links, presence, and analytics are deliberately not carried over") and docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35. The `doc`/`note` arms, which go through serializers, do drop comments — so behavior is also inconsistent between types.

samples.summary: CopySource URL-encodes the bucket/key separator, so the S3/MinIO copy of a blob-backed document likely fails
samples.evidence: `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)` percent-encodes the `/` separators as `%2F`, producing e.g. `wafflebase-files%2Fwafflebase%2Fuuid.pdf`. The S3 contract is "source bucket and key separated by a slash, with the *key name* URL-encoded" — services split the copy-source on the first literal `/` before decoding, so an all-encoded value resolves to no bucket (InvalidArgument / NoSuchBucket). If so, every copy of a pdf/image/file document throws before the row is created and the feature is broken for the three blob types. The new test (file.service.spec.ts) asserts the encoded form against a mocked SDK, so it cannot detect this. Correct form is `${bucket}/${encodeURIComponent(key)}` (or encode each path segment).

samples.summary: Copying a never-opened `doc` document seeds an empty content Tree, defeating the editor's initialRoot paragraph seed and leaving a zero-block copy
samples.evidence: The `doc` arm unconditionally runs `writeDocsRoot(root, content)`; when the source has no content, `readDocsRoot` returns `{ blocks: [] }` (docs-tree.ts:427-431) and `writeDocsRoot` still creates `root.content = new Tree({ type: 'doc', children: [] })` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). Because `content` now exists on the target root, the frontend's `client.attach({ initialRoot: initialDocsRoot() })` (docs-detail.tsx:262) no longer seeds the required first paragraph block — and `initialDocsRoot`'s own comment (types/docs-document.ts:30-36) says a doc without that initial block crashes `text-editor.handleInput` with "Block not found" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:823). The JSON arm explicitly guards this case (`if (Object.keys(snapshot).length === 0) return;`) but the `doc` arm does not. The new spec even asserts the empty write happens (`expect(targetRoot.content).toBeDefined()`).

samples.summary: Copied docs/pdf roots are created without the `comments: {}` container the design explicitly requires to be seeded once
samples.evidence: types/docs-document.ts:38-45 documents that `comments` must be seeded at bootstrap because lazy creation (`if (!root.comments) root.comments = {}`, as done in app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:176) loses a thread when two users add the first comment concurrently (LWW on the container). The copy service creates the target Yorkie doc itself via `writeDocsRoot`, so the root exists before any client attaches; whether the editor's `initialRoot` still backfills the absent `comments` key depends on Yorkie's per-key set-if-absent semantics, which I could not verify (no SDK in the tree). If it does not, every copied docs document permanently lacks the seeded container.

samples.summary: `FileService.copy` uses a stored `fileId` in an object key/CopySource without the `VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN` check the delete path applies
samples.evidence: document.controller.ts:387 guards blob deletion with `doc.fileId && VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN.test(doc.fileId)` before passing a DB-stored id to S3. `DocumentCopyService.copy` (document-copy.service.ts:~76) passes `source.fileId` straight into `fileService.copy`, which interpolates it into `CopySource` with no pattern check — a malformed/legacy id (e.g. containing `/` or `..`) would build a wrong copy source rather than being skipped. Searched: grep for `VALID_FILE_ID_PATTERN` across packages/backend/src (only document.controller.ts and file.constants.ts), and read file.service.ts in full.

samples.summary: Content-copy rollback deletes the DB row and blob but leaves the partially-written Yorkie document behind
samples.evidence: On `copyContent` failure the service deletes the created row and the copied blob, but nothing detaches/removes the target Yorkie key `<prefix><created.id>`, which may already hold a partial `doc.update` that was synced (writeDocsRoot performs multiple root mutations, and the JSON arm assigns keys one by one before sync). The result is an orphan Yorkie document keyed to a nonexistent document id — harmless for correctness of future copies (fresh uuid each time) but a real leak in Yorkie storage, and the rollback comment claims nothing is left behind.

samples.summary: Bulk copy aborts on the first failure and reports only a generic error; the row-menu item is not disabled while a copy is in flight
samples.evidence: `mutationFn: async ({ ids }) => { for (const id of ids) await copyDocument(id); }` throws on the first failing id, so the remaining documents are silently never copied and `onError` shows only "Failed to copy" with no indication of how many succeeded (the list refetch is the only signal). Separately, the row dropdown item at line 982-990 has no `disabled={copyDocumentsMutation.isPending}` (unlike the bulk button at line 1201), so a second click before the first request settles fires another copy and produces an extra `(copy 2)`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. document-copy.service.ts:176-198 copies every key of the source Yorkie root onto the target for sheet/slides/board with no filtering. Spreadsheet comment threads live inside that root: yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-6 stores them at ws.comments (written by applyAddThread, :71-81), and yorkie-store.ts:1304/1317 shows ws === root.sheets[tabId]. prisma/schema.prisma:162 confirms comments exist only inside Yorkie, so there is no other mechanism stripping them. This directly contradicts the service's own contract at document-copy.service.ts:34-36 and docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35 ("Comments ... deliberately not carried over"), and is inconsistent with the doc/note arms (:134-174) which go through readDocsRoot/readNoteRoot serializers that carry no comment fields. The path is reachable unconditionally: copy() calls copyContent at :93, 'sheet' is in JSON_ROOT_TYPES (:27), and the only early return (:187) is the empty-root case. Copied threads carry comment bodies and author usernames into a new document and strand Notification.commentId linkage — a broken invariant / incorrect state propagation in the correctness lane. No guard or caller elsewhere refutes it.

finding.evidence: `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)` percent-encodes the `/` separators as `%2F`, producing e.g. `wafflebase-files%2Fwafflebase%2Fuuid.pdf`. If so, every copy of a pdf/image/file document throws before the row is created and the feature is broken for the three blob types. verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted: file.service.ts:145 sets `CopySource: encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)`, which percent-encodes the bucket/key separator(s) into %2F (two of them when FILE_STORAGE_PREFIX is set, via storageKey() at file.service.ts:63-65). This is not the form any official AWS SDK emits — boto3 percent-encodes CopySource with '/' in the safe set and the Java SDK encodes ignoring slashes, and AWS SDK v3 forwards the string verbatim into the x-amz-copy-source header — so on AWS S3 the value resolves to no bucket (InvalidArgument/NoSuchBucket). The path is live and unguarded: documents.controller.ts:307 -> DocumentCopyService.copy -> document-copy.service.ts:63-65 calls fileService.copy(source.fileId) unconditionally for any blob-backed document, outside the try block that starts at line 68, so the rejection propagates and no row is created — breaking "Make a copy" for pdf/image/file. The endpoint is configurable (file.config.ts:11-12), so AWS S3 is a supported target, not just the dev MinIO in docker-compose.yaml:20-31. The new tests (file.service.spec.ts:166, 181-183) assert the encoded form against a mocked SDK, so they restate the implementation and cannot detect it. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no caller guards it, and a broken core flow is squarely in the correctness lane. Some S3-compatible servers may unescape the whole header before splitting and tolerate this, but I could not demonstrate that from this repository and it would not cover the S3 target, so the uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Copying a never-opened `doc` document seeds an empty content Tree, defeating the editor's initialRoot paragraph seed and leaving a zero-block copy
finding.evidence: The `doc` arm unconditionally runs `writeDocsRoot(root, content)`; when the source has no content, `readDocsRoot` returns `{ blocks: [] }` (docs-tree.ts:427-431) and `writeDocsRoot` still creates `root.content = new Tree({ type: 'doc', children: [] })` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). Because `content` now exists on the target root, the frontend's `client.attach({ initialRoot: initialDocsRoot() })` (docs-detail.tsx:262) no longer seeds the required first paragraph block — and `initialDocsRoot`'s own comment (types/docs-document.ts:30-36) says a doc without that initial block crashes `text-editor.handleInput` with "Block not found" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:823). The JSON arm explicitly guards this case (`if (Object.keys(snapshot).length === 0) return;`) but the `doc` arm does not. The new spec even asserts the empty write happens (`expect(targetRoot.content).toBeDefined()`).

verdict.reason: The code is as quoted (the `doc` arm at document-copy.service.ts:134-152 writes unconditionally, and writeDocsRoot at docs-tree.ts:517-528 does create an empty `content` Tree when readDocsRoot returned `{blocks: []}` at docs-tree.ts:427-431), but the asserted harm is unreachable: the editor bootstrap already handles a zero-block document. `initialize` in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:904-908 checks `docStore.getDocument().blocks.length === 0` and seeds a paragraph via `docStore.setDocument(Doc.create().document)` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:132-136). With an existing-but-empty Tree, YorkieDocStore.getDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:544-568) returns `blocks: []`, so the guard fires; setDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:722-733) -> writeFullDocument (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2640-2707) inserts the paragraph into the empty Tree (childCount 0 -> skip delete, then editBulkByPath) and sets `undoFloor` (enforced by canUndo at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2623-2626), which also covers the undo-unwind hazard cited from docs-document.ts:30-36. This is the real mount path (docs-view.tsx:320-325, also used by shared-document.tsx:838), so `resolveBlockTreePath`'s `Block not found` throw at yorkie-doc-store.ts:823 is not reached. The copy of a never-opened doc is content-identical to its empty source and self-heals to one paragraph on first open, so there is no crash, no data loss, and no blocking correctness defect.
